Indications

No clinical history provided for this patient.

Result

Mutation NO PATHOGENIC MUTATION DETECTED
Mutation Nomenclature -

Interpretation

Patient is negative for ΔF508 (p.Phe508delPhe) mutation in the CFTR gene.

Recommendations

In case of strong suspicion of Cystic Fibrosis, the patient’s sample should be tested for mutations in the entire CFTR gene, as this assay tests only for the most common mutation. Please order CFTR whole gene sequencing for the same.

Test Information

The test is based on the amplification of a human genomic DNA region of CFTR gene containing the most commonly documented mutation delF508 (also known as ΔF508) and subsequent sequencing for detection of mutant alleles.

Methodology

Bi-directional DNA sequencing was carried out using 3500/3730XL Genetic Analyzer Applied Biosystems (ABI) for the common variant delF508 (also known as ΔF508) in the CFTR gene. The data were analyzed using CodonCode Aligner v5.0.2 (CodonCode Corporation, Centerville, MA, USA) and/or Mutation Surveyor v5.0 (Softgenetics, State College, PA, USA).

Limitations

  • Clinical diagnosis and therapy should not be based solely on this assay. The results should be considered in conjunction with clinical information, physical evaluation, and additional diagnostic tests.
  • This test is designed to detect mutations in the above-mentioned regions only. Sequences surrounding the regions of interest are analyzed but not reported.
  • Results have been confirmed by bidirectional sequencing, with the error rate of the Taq polymerase for base incorporation being 1 in 6000 bases.
  • This test has not been approved by external accrediting bodies and has been validated according to internal laboratory criteria. Accreditation is not required for the reporting of these test results.
  • For test performed on specimens received or collected, it is presumed that the specimen belongs to the patient named or identified as labeled on the container/test request and such verification has been carried out at the point of generation of the said specimen by the sender.
